title: Scripting in ZAP: from the Script Console add-on to JSR 223 in core
description: How script support appears in the zap-extensions and zaproxy histories: a Script Console extension in 2012, script support moved into the core in 2013 on javax.script, and the scripts add-on from 2019.
narrative:
A tester who wants to automate checks in ZAP can write them as scripts, and the way ZAP supports scripting has changed several times. A ScriptConsole extension was added to zap-extensions in June 2012.

In July 2013 script support moved into the core, and its new classes import javax.script types such as ScriptEngine and Invocable. In August 2013 the script console was upgraded for languages that are not text based. In February 2014 Custom Input Vector scripting was added.

An announcement in March 2016 indicates that ZAP supported ECMAScript and Zest by default, and that add-ons would extend support to Jython and JRuby. It also said "ZAP will be able to support any language that supports JSR 223".

The scripts add-on was relocated into its own project in April 2019. Its changelog lists moving script types from core under Issue 8027 as unreleased work. The sources cited still show ExtensionScript.java in zaproxy at HEAD. That probably means the split is still in progress.

chapters.title: A ScriptConsole extension, 2012
chapters.text: On 2012-06-25 zap-extensions has the commit "Added the ScriptConsole extension".

chapters.title: Script support moves into the core, 2013
chapters.text: On 2013-07-15 zaproxy has "Issue 735: Move script support into the core". It adds ExtensionScript.java, ScriptEngineWrapper.java, ScriptWrapper.java, ScriptType.java and JavascriptEngineWrapper.java under org/zaproxy/zap/extension/script, active and passive script classes, and ECMAScript templates. The new classes import javax.script types such as ScriptEngine and Invocable.

chapters.title: Languages that are not text, 2013
chapters.text: On 2013-08-02 zaproxy has "Issue 750: Upgrade script console to support non text based scripting languages", and on 2013-08-06 "Allow scripts to override interfaces (Zest support)".

chapters.title: A new script type, 2014
chapters.text: On 2014-02-09 zaproxy has "Added Custom Input Vector scripting capabilities to ZAP".

chapters.title: What ZAP says about JSR 223
chapters.text: The March 2016 newsletter says "By default ZAP supports ECMAScript (JavaScipt) and Zest, a graphical security scripting language from the Mozilla Security team", that add-ons extend support to Jython and JRuby, and "ZAP will be able to support any language that supports JSR 223".

chapters.title: The scripts add-on, 2019 and after
chapters.text: On 2019-04-03 zap-extensions has "scripts: relocate to its own project". The add-on's changelog has, under Unreleased, "Move script types from core (Issue 8027)." At HEAD zaproxy still contains zap/src/main/java/org/zaproxy/zap/extension/script/ExtensionScript.java.
